items.title: Same shape is stronger than a familiar outline
items.student: Draw rectangles R3cm×5cm,S6cm×10cm,T6cm×9cm. Test similarity using corresponding side ratios and angles. Two triangles have side lengths3,4,5and6,8,10;compare with6,8,9. Explain why equal angles alone suffice for triangles but not arbitrary quadrilaterals. Label corresponding vertices/sides consistently. Use clean card/paper models,not personal measurements.
items.teacher: R/Ssimilar with positive linear image/object factor2;Tis not similar toRbecause6/3=2but9/5=1.8. Triangles3,4,5and6,8,10similar by proportional sides;6,8,9fails common ratio. Corresponding angles equal and all corresponding lengths proportional define similarity;rectangles all have right angles but can have different aspect ratios. A change of position/orientation alone does not change shape;distinguish a specified enlargement transformation from similarity in general.

items.title: Locate a centre from corresponding rays
items.student: On equal-unit squared paper draw triangle A(1,1),B(3,1),C(1,2)and image A'(2,2),B'(6,2),C'(2,4). Join and extend AA',BB',CC'. Locate their common centre O,measure two corresponding side ratios,and verify OA'/OAwhere nonzero. Explain why one matched pair alone cannot determine a unique centre/scale factor. Use the supplied blank grid if needed.
items.teacher: CentreO(0,0),k=2. AB2→A'B'4,AC1→A'C'2. Every image vector fromOis2times the original. One pair gives a candidate line but infinitely many centre/factor combinations;at least sufficiently distinct corresponding rays plus scale evidence are needed. Here all three rays meet consistently. Tracing/measurement supports construction but exact coordinate checks avoid relying on ruler error.

items.title: Enlarge and shrink about the origin
items.student: Triangle A(1,1),B(3,1),C(1,3)has centreO(0,0). Construct its image fork=2and separately fork=1/2. Draw rays and label both images. Compare corresponding side ratios and orientation. Explain why k=1/2is a valid positive enlargement transformation that reduces size. This unit excludes negative scale factors;do not use them.
items.teacher: k2images(2,2),(6,2),(2,6);k1/2images(0.5,0.5),(1.5,0.5),(0.5,1.5). Corresponding lengths scale2or0.5;positive factors place images on the same rays from centre and preserve orientation. k1is identity;when object/image coincide,the data do not identify a unique centre. k0collapses a figure and is not used as a similarity here.

items.title: A centre away from the origin
items.student: CentreE(1,−1),triangle A(2,0),B(4,0),C(2,1). Construct image fork=2using E+k(P−E),or equivalent measured rays. Verify every vertex and compare with the incorrect rule P'=2P. Then find the image ofAalone fork=1/2about the sameE. Show why the centre must be used before scaling.
items.teacher: k2:A'(3,1),B'(7,1),C'(3,3). E+k(P−E)is correct;doubling coordinates would mean centreO,notE. Half-sizeAimage(1.5,−0.5). The vector fromEto each image is the stated multiple;don't add a factor to a coordinate. Provide half-unit plotting and a ruler;no negative factors required.

items.title: Why does area scale twice?
items.student: Rectangle2cm×3cm is enlarged byk=3. Find original/image side lengths,perimeters and areas. Tile or sketch the original unit squares to justify the area factor. Audit the claim'if lengths triple,area triples'. For a different similar pair,the original area is20cm² andk=1/2:find image area and explain the ratio direction.
items.teacher: Image6×9cm;perimeters10and30cm;areas6and54cm². Linear/perimeter factor3,area factor9. Both dimensions scale byk,soarea factor k²;20×(1/2)²=5cm². Specify image/object throughout;reversing direction gives reciprocal factors. No assumption that unrelated shapes with those areas are similar.

items.title: Why does volume scale three times?
items.student: Compare ideal cubes of edges2cm and6cm. Find their volumes and total surface areas,and state image/object linear,area and volume factors. Show the volume relation using layers of equal cubes or a labelled product. An ideal cuboid2×3×4cm is enlarged byk=2:find all image dimensions and volume. Explain why scaling only its height would not make a similar solid.
items.teacher: CubesV8,216cm³;surface areas24,216cm²;factors3,9,27. Three dimensions scale,soVfactor k³. Cuboidimage4×6×8cm,V192cm³ versus24cm³,factor8. Height-only change breaks common ratio across corresponding dimensions. Physical card thickness/capacity is considered separately from these ideal geometric volumes.

items.title: Recover a factor and check the similarity assumption
items.student: Similar figures have original/image areas36and81cm²:find positivek. Similar solids have original/image volumes8and125cm³:find positivek. Compare cuboids2×3×4cm and1×4×6cm:do equal volumes prove similarity? Explain why square/cube roots alone cannot establish similarity for shapes not known to be similar. Keep image/object direction explicit.
items.teacher: Area ratio81/36=9/4,k=3/2;volume ratio125/8,k=5/2. Both cuboidsV24but ratios1/2,4/3,3/2are not common,so not similar. Positive root is appropriate because this unit excludes negative factors;finding a candidate scale fromarea/volume assumes a known similarity and does not prove it. Volume cube root may be obtained from recognised cubes/factor reasoning,not an unsupported calculator press.

items.title: What does proportional resizing preserve?
items.student: A fictional photo with width4cm and height6cm must fit a12cm-wide frame with no stretching. Find its proportional height and area factor. A similar model container has capacity250cm³ and linear length ratio model/original=1/5:find the ideal original capacity. A diagram suggests doubling all lengths doubles paint area and storage capacity:repair both claims and state assumptions about material thickness,shape and what is being painted. No liquid filling,climbing or road/shadow measurement is required.
items.teacher: Assume photo width4cm,height6cm:k3,newheight18cm,area factor9. Model/original linear1/5means original/model5;idealcapacity250×125=31,250cm³=31.25L. Doubling similar lengths gives area4andvolume8,not2. Actual usable capacity/material cost may differ due to wall thickness,seams,open surfaces or manufacturing constraints. Frame must be tall enough;do not assume fitting width ensures fitting a fixed height.

items.title: Plan the three container pairs
items.student: Project uses ideal open-top thin-card containers;tabs are additional material,not part of nominal dimensions. Plan cube-shaped containers of edge2and4cm;cuboids with bases2×3and4×6cm,heights4and8cm;cylinders of radius1.4and2.8cm,heights3and6cm. Fork=2predict area/volume factors. For cube/cuboid draw a cross net:base with one height-sized wall attached to each corresponding base edge. For cylinder use a base circle plus wall rectangle of circumference×height. Useπ=22/7for the paper-template dimensions. Record required materials,measurements and likely sources of error before construction.
items.teacher: All pairsk2,idealarea factor4andvolume factor8. Cube/cuboid wall widths must match the base edge to which attached;cube2base2×2,four2×2walls;large4×4,four4×4walls. Cuboid base2×3,two2×4walls,two3×4walls;largebase4×6,two4×8,two6×8walls. Cylinderwall8.8×3and17.6×6cm,base diameters2.8/5.6cm;teacherprecutcircles. Add labelled glue/tape tabs outside all dimensions,allow drying and keep openings unblocked. Idealvolumes cube8/64,cuboid24/192,cylinder18.48/147.84cm³ usingstatedπ;do not claim exact real capacity from outer dimensions.

items.title: Construct,measure and document
items.student: In a group construct the three similar container pairs from your checked SE9 plan using clean reused card,teacher-precut pieces,tape and approved blunt scissors. Record each person's actual contribution,all nominal and measured dimensions,and any seam/thickness mismatch. Compare ratios with intendedk=2without pretending measurements are exact. Keep containers dry;no food or liquid use. If construction cannot be done,mark PLANNED,NOT CONSTRUCTED;drawings do not prove making the containers.
items.teacher: Teacher checks nets before cutting,provides pre-cut circles/tabs and capacity-appropriate station roles. Observe actual construction/measurement for named learners;the group product alone does not establish each learner made all6containers. Avoid sharp wire,glass,hot glue,food waste and unapproved tools. Ratio deviations can arise from ruler precision,folds,tabs and wall thickness;record actual values,not teacher ideal answers. Store clean finished containers for later learning and sort/reuse scraps responsibly. Extend construction time when required rather than falsely marking finished.

items.title: Digital resize and project evidence audit
items.student: With a teacher-approved drawing/photo tool,resize a2×3rectangle by positivek=2andk=1/2using locked aspect ratio. Record the actual tool,settings and resulting dimensions;compare unlocked-width-only resizing. Photograph or video only the containers/work,not people or personal information,and save with a clear project filename if devices permit. Share measurements,challenges and one practical use/limit. If no device,make a labelled paper comparison and mark digital resize/capture/save NOT OBSERVED. Audit the claim'our group has shown every learner can use the tool'.
items.teacher: Locked-aspect results4×6and1×1.5in the tool's declared units;area factors4and1/4. Unlockedwidth-only scaling distorts unless both corresponding dimensions share one factor. Teacher supplies approved access/no account or personal data;records actual observed actions for each learner,not inferred from group display. Source project asks documentation/capture/save;paper alternative supports maths while digital evidence remains pending. Record project dimensions/challenges honestly and state a supported practical benefit without claiming an enduring attitude change.

items.title: Independent similarity data
items.student: Fresh data for final prompts. Triangle A(2,2),B(4,2),C(2,3)has image A'(3,3),B'(7,3),C'(3,5)under a positive enlargement. Another pointD(3,4)is to use that same transformation. PhotoP3cm×4cm,photoQ6cm×8cm,photoR6cm×7cm. An ideal similar container pair has original volume12cm³ and linear image/original factor2. A separate similar figure pair has original area40cm² and positivek=1/2. Use equal-unit squared paper and these data only. No teaching cards,project models,worked examples or peer discussion during assessment. For triangle areas,take one coordinate unit as1cm;grid lines are equally spaced.
items.teacher: P/Qsimilar factork2;P/Rnotcommonratio. TrianglecentreE(1,1),k2;D'(5,7). Joining correspondingrays and side ratios supportscentre;[A'−E]=2[A−E],etc. Half-sizeimageofDaboutEis(2,2.5),if asked separately. TriangleAB2→A'B'4,AC1→A'C'2;area1→4cm²ifgridunit1cm. Containerimagevolume96cm³,volumefactor8,areafactor4. Separatehalf-scalearea10cm². Negativefactorsoutsideunit. Realcontainercapacityneedsinternaldimensions/thickness/actualmeasurement;writtenfinaldoesnotcertifyconstruction/digitalactions.
